Where the relocation loop really starts. As the level is loaded, $7EC3-$7EC4 hold LDA #$00, so the count at $1E starts from zero here; once every pointer is done, $7ECE-$7ED0 write RTS ($60) over that LDA, so in a snapshot taken during play $7EC3 reads RTS and $7EC4 keeps the old $00.

EngineEntry: The Final Battle's play code starts here, from PhaseHandoff at $3FF3. It sets $AA to $FF, which lets the interrupt routine play the tune, relocates the scene pointers, clears the scene buffers, waits 25 ticks, lowers the sprite curtain over the play window (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), draws the credits card, sets the background to black, raises the curtain again and waits until it is gone (RaiseSpriteCurtain, $8536), which shows the card, then waits for the fire button or the second button read through the SID's pot X ($D419), keeping which in $AC, and goes on into EnterArea ($83AA) and the main loop. Central Park's EngineEntry also sets $03CB to 1; this one leaves it alone.

Reinitialize the Final Battle playable phase's scene buffers after GAME OVER and rejoin engine startup immediately before the common gameplay-entry tail. Its one caller is $8506, reached when the last life is lost and no spare life is left.
Inputs: The death sequence has finished; resident state and the active phase occupant remain valid.
Outputs: Calls the phase scene-buffer initializer, clears $D021 to black, redraws the credit/title card (RenderCreditTitleCard, $82BB, which clears the play window first), and continues at the engine's input/frame-loop setup at $838F.

Set up the current area and enter the main loop, for The Final Battle. This runs once each time an area is entered or redrawn, not once a frame: it is reached by falling through from the start-up wait at $83A8, from MainTick when the redraw latch $02A9 is set ($8462) and after a lost life ($84C9), and it falls into MainTick ($8404), the per-tick loop.
Inputs: Current area $A2, the player's position and the actor/object state.
Outputs: Sets $0230=$7F; rebuilds the area's enemy meter when $012D,X holds $80-$FE and loads $022A from the area's enemy energy at $3F92; clears the play window and draws the area's scene ($89CC); clears the actor slots, resets runtime state, compiles the collision records, spawns the enemy, draws inactive objects and composes the actors; on the first visit to an area below $12 sets its $011B byte and adds a score bonus ($1183 with A=$15); redraws the HUD digits, applies the area's entrance rules ($892A), stamps $026D from $E2, sets $0230=$FF and falls into MainTick.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $0230, gameplay zero page, actor/object/projectile arrays, renderer/collision scratch, and display work state.
Hardware: Through its helpers, writes $D021 and the VIC-II-visible bitmap, screen and colour memory.

ResolveLevelCompletion: runs when the completion request $02AF is set. In this level it asks for no items. Then it adds 5,000 points to the score ($1183 with A = $50: 5 to the thousands digit, 0 to the hundreds), saves the items, score and clock for the next level (SaveLevelState, $1C30), counts the energy $0229 up from 0 to 21, one step each time the interrupt routine changes $022B, and jumps to the load coordinator at $16AD for the next part.

Inputs: $0232 is the curtain's lower edge (a raster line, which AnimateStatusPanelReveal at $1F75 lowered) and the interrupt owns the $0231 handshake. Outputs: $0232 is reduced, two lines a frame, below $1D, sprite X expansion is disabled and $0231 is cleared, so the interrupt stops drawing the curtain. Called at the start of the game ($837E), after a lost life ($84C3) and after GAME OVER ($84FE). Clobbers: A, flags, $0231, and $0232. Hardware: writes VIC-II sprite X-expansion register $D01D.

Take the exit at the edge of the current area; MainTick calls it once a tick, and it does nothing while $0234 is non-zero. Inputs: $0234, current area $A2, player position $54 (across) and $55 (down), and the exit thresholds at $86E2. Outputs: when the player is at an edge (Y below 9, Y $BD or more, X $F7 or more, or X below 2) the position becomes a place on the area's edge, counted clockwise from the top left: a quarter of the distance along the edge, plus 0 on the top, $3D on the right, $6A on the bottom and $A7 on the left. The first exit of the area's group in $86E2 whose threshold is above that place is installed through InstallSceneStateRecordX ($8694), which moves the player to the destination area and position, or sets the level-exit request $02AF=$FF when the destination is $FF. Away from the edges it returns without change. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install record 0, the level's starting place, as the selected spawn: it loads X with 0 and falls into InstallSceneStateRecordX, whatever the current room. In Final Battle record 0 is area 1 at X $58, Y $5A, heading 3. Its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($82A8). Inputs: none. Outputs: $0278=0, and the area, player position, heading, command and redraw latches from record 0. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and the installed area/player state.

Install the Final Battle scene-state/spawn record selected by X.
Inputs: X indexes parallel area, player-coordinate, heading, and command-state arrays at $86E6/$86EA/$86EE/$86F2; callers have already resolved the transition variant and any $0234 gate.
Outputs: A $FF area byte sets $02AF=$FF and returns; otherwise stores X in $0278 and installs area $A2, player coordinates $54/$55/$028E/$028F/$74, heading $68/$69, derived pose $65, command $81, and redraw latches $02A9/$02B8.
Clobbers: A, X, processor flags, $0278, $02AF on the sentinel path, and the installed area/player/redraw state; Y is preserved.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Load the selected Final Battle spawn record into active area, player-position, facing, and transition state
Inputs: $0278 = selected record index; parallel Final Battle area, X, Y, and packed facing/state tables
Outputs: $A2 = area; $54/$028E = X; $55/$74/$028F = Y; $68/$69 = heading; $65 = $10 or $11 facing-image selector; $81 = packed byte shifted right four; $02A9/$02B8 = $FF; A = $FF; X = selected index
Clobbers: A, X, and processor flags; Y is preserved

4 bytes of exit thresholds. Byte 0 belongs to no area: the scans start at byte 1, and entry 0 of the four tables that follow is the level's start position. Then comes a group for each area, closed by $FF. The routine that finds the exit the player is walking through skips a group for each area before the current one, turns the player's place on the edge of the play window into one number running clockwise round it from the top left, and takes the first value in the group above that number, the closing $FF included. The same index then selects the exit's destination in the four tables that follow.

4 exits, $86E6-$86E9: the area it leads to, or $FF for the way out of the level (entry 2, the first exit of area 1's group, reached from area 1's top edge left of X 34), which sets the level-exit request $02AF instead of moving the player. Values: 0, 1, 255, 0.
4 exits, $86EA-$86ED: the X position the player arrives at. Values: 12, 49, 255, 214.
4 exits, $86EE-$86F1: the Y position the player arrives at. Values: 133, 176, 255, 92.
4 exits, $86F2-$86F5: the heading in the low three bits, and a command in the high nibble. Values: 1, 1, 255, 5.

The player's death, once the fall is over: it clears $F2, crumbles the sprites away (DissolveSpriteImages, $A55C), lowers the sprite curtain over the play window again (AnimateStatusPanelReveal, $1F75), waits 25 ticks (WaitEngineTicks, $99F9), clears the play window ($140E), sets the background to black and takes one from the lives, item 26's flag at $03F2. The caller tests the Z flag that the DEC leaves: with no lives left it spends a spare life, item 8, if the player has one, and otherwise the game is over. Clobbers: A, X, Y and flags.
Impose a short fixed CPU delay. Inputs: none. Outputs: X ends at zero after 128 countdown iterations. Clobbers: X and flags; A and Y are preserved.

Reset The Final Battle's transient control, actor, object, animation, and AI state to its fixed entry sentinels when the level starts or restarts: its one caller is InitSceneBuffers ($82AF), not the area set-up. Inputs: No register arguments; the Final Battle playable occupant and shared zero-page workspace are active. Outputs: Stores $FF to $6C, $02B8, and $84; stores zero to $78, $02AF, $61, $63, $64, $66, $9F, $B3, $B6, $B4, $72, $F2, $7D, $BF, and $0279; stores $D2 to $86; A returns $D2. Clobbers: A, N, and Z plus the listed RAM state; X, Y, C, and V are preserved.

Sample and normalize gameplay input and process edge-triggered interface controls for The Final Battle. Inputs: active-low control-port-2 state, control-port-1/keyboard state, keyboard-select table `$1DA5`, previous edge latches, and current interface state. Outputs: `$7C` bits 0–4 from control-port-2 direction/fire and bit 5 from the POTX threshold, raw keyboard rows `$0260-$0267`, edge latches `$02AA-$02AE/$02BF`, and phase interface/action state. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and scanner/interface scratch. Hardware: writes `$FF`, keyboard-row masks, and `$80` to CIA 1 port A `$DC00`; reads `$DC00`, CIA 1 port B `$DC01`, and SID POTX `$D419`; on the F1 edge that switches the music off (`$AA` flipped to zero) it clears SID registers `$D400-$D417`.
The Final Battle adds this: no pause key during the ending
The Final Battle adds this: no MODE key during the ending

Text "MODE  ", drawn by the call at $88B8 that comes before it: column 17, row 20, colours $03 and $E6, then 6 glyph numbers (0 a space, 1-26 A-Z, 27-36 the digits) and a zero. The second space, at $88C4, is a placeholder: the instruction at $88B5 writes the mode $03F3 (0 to 2) plus $1C into it before the call, so the line reads MODE 1, MODE 2 or MODE 3. The routine returns to the instruction after the zero, at $88C6.
Text 88bb plus 9, the address the instruction at $88B5 writes: byte 9 of the table at $88BB.
The text routine at $1583 returns here, to the first instruction after the zero that ends "MODE" at $88C5, and the routine that called it at $88B8 goes on.
The Final Battle adds this: no quitting or pausing during the ending

Initial sequence byte zero and the current-value indexed base for the hidden-input recognizer at $88FC. Together with the next-byte alias $8918 it stores 19 values $8917-$8929; the scanner advances $BF only when normalized input matches the expected change. After the 18th matched change it sets $02AF=$FF, the request to end the level.
Expected next value of the 19-byte control sequence beginning at $8917, read with the current progress X at $8901. This is an overlapping indexed base, not another allocated array.

Apply the entrance rules for the exit the player arrived by and for the current area. Inputs: $0278, the exit record the player arrived by (an index into the tables at $86E6 on), and the current area $A2. Outputs: the entrance animation's kind and length from the list at $8998 go to $0293/$0294 (kind 0 when $0278 is not listed); exit $17 sets $74=$98 and $EF=$FF; in area $0D with item flag $03E9 set, the first collision coordinate is copied ($F460 to $F462) and it returns; otherwise InitializeRoomSpecificEntranceState installs the AI scripts and sprite colours of areas $0A, $0E, $0F, $10 and $11. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI-script state. Hardware: writes the sprite multicolour registers $D025/$D026 directly in areas $0A, $0E, $10 and $11.

The Final Battle's own entrance rules: only area 1, the room with the five candles, has any. Until flag $03E9 is set (item 17, object record 0) it draws scene $898C, the panel shut; after that $8990, the panel raised, and then the lock: scene $8994 until item 18 is held (the code entered, ObjectEnterCode at $B327), then $B467, the lock open, or $B46E once item 16 has been taken out (ObjectSummonKunitoki at $B3ED). Object records 1 and 2 draw the same $B467 and $B46E when they are taken (and record 4 $B467); record 0 draws $B442 instead, which raises the panel in five steps and leaves it, with the lock, where $8990 and $8994 draw them.
Scene 13 at column 21, row 0, ending with $FF: the panel in area 1 before item 17 is taken.
Scene 13 at column 21, five rows higher (row -5), ending with $FF: the panel raised.
Scene 19 at column 22, row 5, ending with $FF: the lock behind the panel, shut.

The Final Battle's entrance-animation list, three bytes an entry as in Central Park's (the spawn record the player arrived by, the kind of entrance, how many animation steps it lasts), ending with $FF. This level's has no entries: only the $FF.

Mark all eight actor slots inactive and clear their key state bytes. Inputs: none. Outputs: $61, $63, and the corresponding $0210 and $0248 slot arrays are cleared. Clobbers: A is zero, Y exits as $FF, and flags change; X is preserved.

The address ApplySceneEntryRules reads the third byte of an entrance-animation entry from ($8940, with X stepping by three). With the list at $8998 empty the read never happens here; the address is the operand of ClearActorSlots's first instruction, as $8999, where the second byte would be read, is its opcode.

Copy the 1000-byte screen-color staging image into C64 color RAM. Inputs: staging bytes $0800-$0BE7 and visible C64 I/O. Outputs: color RAM $D800-$DBE7 receives the corresponding low nybbles; the last 24 cells of the third page are harmlessly copied twice. Clobbers: A, X, and flags; X returns zero. Hardware: writes color RAM $D800-$DBE7.

Provide The Final Battle's reserved per-tick runtime hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing gameplay state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

Provide The Final Battle's reserved presentation-initialization hook. Inputs: A normal JSR return address on the stack. Outputs: Returns immediately without changing presentation state. Clobbers: Registers and flags are preserved; RTS consumes the normal return address.

RTS: where The Final Battle's title load points PlayNextLoadVector at $3FF6. The one call through that vector, from StartLevelLoad (engine $1405), comes once as the game starts, before any level is loaded, and goes through the engine's own JMP $0E00 there, so this RTS is never reached.
RenderConditionalSceneVariant: The Final Battle draws the plain scene of the current area ($A2) every time, with none of the variants Central Park chooses with its flags.

When the player's level-condition latch is active and no player animation script is running, force zero health and install the facing-specific terminal animation
Inputs: condition latch $B6, player animation-pointer high byte $61, and facing byte $69; animation streams begin at $B629 and $B61D
Outputs: sets player health $0229=0 and tail-installs one of the two terminal animation streams; otherwise returns unchanged
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and the state changed by InstallAnimation

Hide the parts of an actor's sprites that are behind the current area's foreground pictures, then stage the sprites. Inputs: X is the first sprite slot to process (0 for the player, 4 for the other actor, or an auxiliary slot); it works up to slot 3, or slot 7 when X is 4 or more. A is the actor's depth ($74 or $74,X), compared with byte 1 of each 4-byte record in the area's list (pointers at $9186, an $FF ends a list; a record is a picture's scene index, a depth, a column and a row). Outputs: for each drawn slot ($0218 bit 4 or 6 set, $0210 non-zero), every record whose depth is at least A is tested by TestSceneConditionRecord ($8AA9): where the picture overlaps the 24-by-21 sprite, the sprite's pixel pairs under the picture's non-zero pixels are cleared and $0218 bit 4 is set. Then, with interrupts off, each slot with $0218 bit 6 gets its position, pointer ($30 or $38 plus the slot) and colour bits staged in $0240, $0258 and $0250, and $0210 is copied to $0248. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and masking scratch.

Mask one foreground picture out of a sprite slot. Inputs: ($ED) points at the area's list of 4-byte records (scene index, depth, column, row) and Y at the depth byte of one of them; $1F is the sprite slot, and $F4/$F6 and $F5 its X (low and high bytes) and Y. Outputs: the record's picture is placed at column x 8 and row x 8 + $1A, with the width and height from its header byte; if it does not overlap the 24-by-21 sprite the routine returns at once, otherwise it sets bit 4 of the slot's $0218 and clears, in the slot's sprite image, every pixel pair that lies under a non-zero pixel pair of the picture. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $04-$07, $1C/$1D, $21/$22, $25/$26, $8C/$8D, $D7-$DB and the slot's sprite image.

24 entries: eight zeroes, eight ones and eight twos, read at $8BD7, $8BED, $8C03 and $8C19 with the clipped horizontal pixel position as the index: which of the three bytes of a sprite row a pixel pair falls in. Paired with the clearing masks at $8C8D. Central Park's table is at $99A3.

24 entries: $3F, $3F, $CF, $CF, $F3, $F3, $FC, $FC, three times, one set for each byte of a sprite row, read at $8BDC, $8BF2, $8C08 and $8C1E. The scene-condition renderer ANDs the mask into the chosen sprite-row byte wherever the scene's pixel pair is not zero, which clears that pair from the sprite. Central Park has one more byte after its copy of this table ($99D3, a zero); here code follows at once.

PlayEnding, where MainTick goes once $02B9 is set (Kunitoki down inside the candles with all five lit, at $9CC2 or $B271). It adds 5,000 points to the score ten times, 50,000 in all ($1183 with A = $50), and redraws the panel, copies the six score digits ($1CA0) into the TOTAL SCORE text at $8F2F and the clock's hours, minutes and seconds (glyphs $1C77, $1C81 and $1C8B, two each) into the TOTAL TIME text at $8F4F, $8F52 and $8F55, sets both energies $0229 and $022A to zero and clears $012E, area 1's enemy record.

Until the player has captured the spirit, the game runs on: the player can move and act (PlayerDriver, ScheduleEnemyAnimation, EventDispatch), the floor colours cycle (CycleEndingColours) and the candles flicker (FlickerCandles), and EndingFrame fills and empties both energy bars. Each time Kunitoki's animation ends ($63 zero) it is started again from $C1AD, frames 122 down to 105 and then 100, after which it goes on at $C17A, frames 105 back up to 123, unless flag $03EF is set (item 23, ObjectCaptureSpirit at $B430).

The spirit captured: it fixes both energies at what the bars show ($022B and $022C), hides the player's four sprites ($0248-$024B) and clears the screen and its colour RAM (each colour byte is written twice) except columns 10-20 of rows 9, 10 and 15, columns 0-29 of rows 11 and 12, columns 0-25 of rows 13 and 14, columns 10-15 of row 16 and columns 31-39 of rows 21 to 23, with the background $D021 black. Then it prints CONGRATULATIONS, YOU HAVE CAPTURED THE SPIRIT OF THE EVIL SHOGUN KUNITOKI, MAY IT NEVER AGAIN BE UNLEASHED, TOTAL SCORE and TOTAL TIME with their figures, from the texts that follow.

EndingLoop, which never ends: once each count of the interrupt counter $E2 it runs the enemy's animation, CycleEndingColours, FlickerCandles and RuntimeNoOpHook, and, as EndingFrame does, sets $029D to 1 and $029C to 0 whenever $029D is not zero, so the countdown at $029C-$029D is held at 256 or less. The game stops here; only a reset leaves it.

EndingFrame: waits for the next count of the interrupt counter $E2. When both energy bars have caught up with their energies ($0229 equal to $022B and $022A to $022C), it sets both energies to $2C less the enemy's, so they go from 0 to $2C and back, and the bars fill and empty in turn. When $029D is not zero it sets $029D to 1 and $029C to 0. The pair is a countdown, $029D the high byte, which the interrupt routine decrements at $1E42-$1E4A, so it is held at 256 or less; besides that decrement, only this test ($8FAA) and the same one in EndingLoop ($8F64) read $029D.

CycleEndingColours, once every few interrupt counts (GateUpdateByTickInterval with X = 5): it steps $022D through the eight colours at $917D and, in the cells between the candles (row 10 and row 11 from column 11 to 20, row 12 from 8 to 22, row 13 from 4 to 24, rows 14 and 15 from 12 to 17, row 16 from 13 to 15), repaints every pixel of the previous colour in the next one: in the colour RAM copy at $0800 and colour RAM itself, and in both nibbles of the screen bytes. A shape drawn in the first colour, red, glows through orange and the greys and back.
The colours CycleEndingColours steps through: 2, 8, 11, 12, 15, 12, 11, 8 (red, orange, dark grey, grey, light grey, grey, dark grey, orange). The ninth byte, 0, is never read: the index wraps at 8.

FlickerCandles, called from MainTick every pass ($8440, a call Central Park's MainTick does not make) and from the ending's loops at $8CF6 (EndingWaitForCapture) and $8F79 (EndingLoop): at most every 6 counts of the interrupt counter $E2 (the last time kept in $03EC), and only in area 1, it redraws each lit candle ($029F-$02A3 negative) with the other flame: it flips bit 0 of the candle's byte and draws scene 32 or 33 at the candle's place from the tables at $92A3 and $92A8, through the one-placement scene at $B475.

The five candles' rows as scene placement bytes (row plus 14): 15, 12, 9, 9 and 12.

Advance the scripted animation attached to a boundary event. Inputs: actor activity $61, sequence state $0293, and countdown $0294. Outputs: the timer and state advance and the selected animation may be installed. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state.

Conditionally dispatch the pending script command through the Final Battle target-minus-one table
Inputs: command/state bytes $80/$81 and player animation-pointer high byte $61; $80 low six bits select the command; the target-minus-one words start at $9341 and are read from the base $933F with X = twice the command
Outputs: when $81 is negative and the bit-6/$61 gate admits it, transfers to the selected command handler by RTS dispatch; command zero or a failed gate returns normally
Clobbers: A, X, flags and two stack bytes before dispatch; Y is preserved until the selected handler

RTS completing the stack-built dispatch at $9338. The high-byte indexed load uses this address as its base with X=2*command, so nonzero commands read the high bytes of target-minus-one words beginning at $9341. This byte is executable RTS, not the start of a standalone pointer array. Command zero returns before dispatch.

Return at once, for the script commands that have no action. Its RTS returns to the code that called ScriptDispatch: the address the dispatcher pushed was used up by the RTS at $9340 that jumped here. Inputs and outputs: none. Clobbers: nothing.

Run the heading-7, state-$70-zero scripted animation sequence, then consume the pending command.

Outputs: On heading 7 with $70 zero, runs one $B6A9 animation, two $B6AE animations, then $B6C3, sets $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $98 and $EF to $FF, which holds it there, and calls resident pacing $11F1; always clears $81 before returning.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $9E and hold it there ($EF = $FF stops ApplySignedActorHeightDelta changing it), then run the common eight-cycle fatal sequence.

Outputs: Stores $74=$9E and $EF=$FF, then runs eight cycles and sets death latch $B6=$FF.

Copy the player's Y ($55) into $74, the Y the scene conditions test, and run the common eight-cycle fatal sequence.
Inputs: Player Y $55 (its whole-pixel byte; $51 holds the fraction) and current animation/actor state.
Outputs: Stores $55 into $74, then runs eight cycles and sets death latch $B6=$FF.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and $B6.

Advance eight scripted animation/update cycles and latch player death.
Inputs: $74 and $EF as the script left them, and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Calls $94C7 with A=8, which marks $0234 and advances eight cycles, then writes $B6=$FF.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to 0, run two scripted animation/update cycles and then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A), which takes two points of the player's energy; then consume the command.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=0 and enters the two-cycle entry at $944B, whose tail calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer; both paths clear $81 before return.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $5D, hold it there with $EF = $FF, advance one scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A), which takes two points of the player's energy.
Inputs: Current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Stores $74=$5D and $EF=$FF, calls the one-cycle path through $94C7, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears command $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Advance 1 scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A), which takes two points of the player's energy, then consume the pending command.
Inputs: $74 and $EF as the script left them, and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Calls $94C7 with A=1; after the bounded loop, calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears $81 and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Command $1A loads $5D, then branches to $9441 to store it in $74, the Y the scene conditions test, set $EF=$FF and run one scripted update cycle and then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, before clearing command $81. This entry shares that tail with the $00 and $7D variants; it differs from $942B in its branch path.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $00, hold it there with $EF = $FF, advance one scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A), which takes two points of the player's energy.
Inputs: Current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Stores $74=$00 and $EF=$FF, calls the one-cycle path through $94C7, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears command $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $7D, hold it there with $EF = $FF, advance one scripted animation/update cycle and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A), which takes two points of the player's energy.
Inputs: Current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Stores $74=$7D and $EF=$FF, calls the one-cycle path through $94C7, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears command $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Command $12 loads A=1 and branches to the bounded update loop at $9451. $74 and $EF stay as the script left them; the tail calls $94C7 once, then ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, and clears $81. Unlike the target-setting entries, this entry writes neither $74 nor $EF itself.

Advance 2 scripted animation/update cycles and run ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A), which takes two points of the player's energy, then consume the pending command.
Inputs: $74 and $EF as the script left them, and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Calls $94C7 with A=2; after the bounded loop, calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand ($950A) with X=$F8 and Y=4, which it does not read: it takes two points of the player's energy $0229 through DamagePlayer, then clears $81 and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0229, $0234, and animation/actor scratch; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Script command 13: plays the player's facing animation four times through, running the engine until each one ends (RepeatScriptRuntimeFrames, A = 4), then, where Central Park runs its scripted coordinate sequence with X = $F8 and Y = 4, calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $950A, so the player loses two points of energy. It clears the command $81 and returns. The Final Battle has no copy of that sequence; every call that went to it goes to $950A here. No wall in The Final Battle carries command 13, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

When command bit 0 is set, run seven scripted cycles and enter the common death-latch tail; otherwise only clear the command.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path calls $94C7 with A=7 then writes $B6=$FF; unarmed path clears $81 without damage.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $04, hold it there with $EF = $FF, run seven cycles, and latch death.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=$04/$EF=$FF and enters the seven-cycle fatal tail; unarmed path clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

When command bit 0 is set, set $74, the Y the scene conditions test, to $0C, hold it there with $EF = $FF, run seven cycles, and latch death.
Inputs: Command flags $81 and current actor/animation state.
Outputs: Armed path stores $74=$0C/$EF=$FF and enters the seven-cycle fatal tail; unarmed path clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $74, $EF, $81, $0234, animation/actor scratch, and on the armed path $B6.

Run The Final Battle's fixed animation at $B6F4 the requested number of times, run the finishing animation at $B709 once, then synchronize three engine-tick stamps. Inputs: A is a nonzero repetition count; animation streams $B6F4 and $B709, actor state, the blocking runtime loop, and resident tick-snapshot helper $11F1 are active. Outputs: Each $B6F4 cycle is installed and serviced until $61 clears; $B709 is then installed and serviced once; finally $026C, $026E, and $0277 receive the current engine tick $E2 and A returns that tick. Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, transient stack contents, animation/runtime state, and $026C/$026E/$0277. Hardware: Through the blocking runtime loop, advances sprite/display state and reads controls; this wrapper and the $11F1 timer-snapshot tail perform no direct I/O.

Install an animation and run the blocking script runtime loop. Inputs: A:X is the animation pointer and the actor context is valid. Outputs: the animation is installed and the runtime loop completes. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and runtime state. Hardware: changes sprite presentation indirectly through the engine.

Run script-time engine frames until the active actor or action completes. Inputs: an installed animation and valid runtime state. Outputs: enemy AI, auxiliary sprites, input, and animation state advance until $61 clears. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and broad frame scratch. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly and reads input through the called joystick poller.

Advance the player's and then the enemy's animation by one eligible engine step, at most once a tick. Inputs: tick $E2 and timer slot 2 ($026A, interval 1 at $95E8); both actors' animation state. Outputs: when no tick has passed since the last call the gate at $95D2 returns straight to RunScriptRuntimeLoop; otherwise AnimationInterpreter ($990A, X=0) steps the player's animation, and ScheduleEnemyAnimation ($98F5) steps the enemy's when its own tick has advanced. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation scratch.

Execute a scripted action for a fixed number of completed animation cycles. Inputs: A is the repetition count and actor facing and animation state are valid. Outputs: the count is exhausted and scripted state advances. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, stack, and $0234. Hardware: changes sprite and display state indirectly.

Install one of two player-animation descriptors selected from the current facing direction. Inputs: Player facing $69 and Final Battle animation descriptors $C01B and $C024. Outputs: A:X contains the selected descriptor and control tail-transfers to InstallAnimation, which initializes $60/$61, $5C, $58, $96, and $5D. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and animation state through the tail-called installer.

Script command 31. Where Central Park tests its clearance predicate here and then runs its scripted coordinate sequence, The Final Battle calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $950A instead. That returns with A zero, so this always goes on to $9500, which sets X to $07 and Y to 2 (values only the missing sequence would have read) and goes on into the same routine again: the player loses two points of energy twice and the command is cleared. No wall in The Final Battle carries command 31, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Script command 30. Where Central Park tests its clearance predicate here and then runs its scripted coordinate sequence, The Final Battle calls ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $950A instead. That returns with A zero, so this always goes on to $9506, which sets X to $0E and Y to 0 (values only the missing sequence would have read) and goes on into the same routine again: the player loses two points of energy twice and the command is cleared. No wall in The Final Battle carries command 30, and the walls are the only source of commands, so it never runs in this level.

Sets X to $07 and Y to 2 and goes on to ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $950A, which ignores them: Central Park's scripted coordinate sequence, which would have read them, is not in this level.

Sets X to $0E and Y to 0 and goes on to ScriptDamagePlayerTwoAndClearCommand at $950A, which ignores them: Central Park's scripted coordinate sequence, which would have read them, is not in this level.

Apply two units of player damage and consume the pending script command.
Inputs: Player energy $0229 and command $81.
Outputs: Calls DamagePlayer with A=2, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, flags, $0229 and $81; when the energy runs out, also $6D and the death latch $B6.

Request enemy projectile type 2 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=2 to $A84C; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 3 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=3 to $A84C; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 4 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=4 to $A84C; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Request enemy projectile type 5 through the fixed second projectile slot and consume the pending command.
Inputs: Enemy position/heading $56/$57/$6B, projectile slot 1 state $0281/$0283/$0285/$0287/$0289, and command $81.
Outputs: Passes A=5 to $A84C; if slot 1 is free and the derived coordinate is in range it initializes the slot, then clears $81.
Clobbers: A, X, flags, projectile slot-1 fields, $0296, and $81.

Advance the player actor for the elapsed IRQ ticks, selecting control, script, animation, movement, collision, and logical-sprite work
Inputs: tick $E2/$026C, timed-event state $0293, player script pointer $60/$61, movement/action state $50/$51,$54/$55,$5C,$65,$68/$69,$70,$79,$89, and normalized input $7C
Outputs: stamps elapsed delta in $8F and $026C; advances timed events or control/script state; updates player coordinates, motion/pose/action, collision state, and logical sprite component buffers
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-driver, movement, collision, animation, and sprite-composition scratch

Compose the player's image and hide the parts behind the area's foreground pictures. Inputs: desired direction $68 (its bit from $1DA5 goes to $1E), facing $69, frame $65, depth $74 and the current area's foreground list. Outputs: logical sprite slots 0-3 hold frame $65, mirrored for facing indexes 1 and 3 (the flags at $9B29); ComposeSprites clears $9F; MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots in $0240-$025F. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E, and compositor and masking scratch. Hardware: changes sprite or image RAM; no VIC-II register is written directly.

Compose the Final Battle playable phase's player frame $65 into logical actor slot 0, mirrored when the facing flag at $9B29,X ANDed with $1E is non-zero.
Inputs: X is the facing index ($69 shifted right once) into the four mirror flags at $9B29; $1E is the direction bit of $68; $65 is the frame; player position/facing and sprite work buffers are current.
Outputs: Passes $9B29,X AND $1E to ComposeSprites as the mirror flag, with X=0 and Y=$65, composes logical actor slot 0, then falls through to $95CB, which masks the player's sprites behind the area's foreground pictures.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, sprite-composition scratch/buffers, and masking scratch.
Hardware: No direct VIC-II register write; the composition helper updates sprite work buffers and changes $01 transiently before restoring it.

Mask the Final Battle playable phase's player sprites, actor slot 0, against the area's foreground pictures without recomposing its frame.
Inputs: Player sprite slots 0-3 are composed; $74 supplies the vertical coordinate compared with each foreground record's depth byte; the area's foreground list (pointers at $9186) is current.
Outputs: Sets X=0, loads A=$74, and tail-enters MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery ($89F2), which clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots' positions, pointers and colours in $0240-$025F.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, and masking scratch; the slots' positions are read from $0200/$0208/$0210.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Rate-limit an update and abort its caller when the slot's minimum interval has not passed. Inputs: X timer slot (2 for the script loop's animation step, 5 for DrawActiveObject, 9 and 10 for the two auxiliary sprite slots, 12 for OpponentAI), global tick $E2, per-slot stamp $0268,X, and threshold table $95E6. Outputs: the eligible path updates timing state; the ineligible path returns to the caller's caller. Clobbers: A, flags, timing state, and two stack bytes on the abort path.

16 slot-indexed minimum intervals. $95D5 subtracts the slot's last tick $0268,X from current $E2, $95D8 compares the difference to this table and the gate discards the caller return frame when too soon; accepted calls update the saved tick. Most intervals are 1, with exceptions 6,2 and4 in the captured table; the slots this level uses are 2, 5, 9, 10 and 12, so the 2 at slot 7 is not read.

Translate the normalized Final Battle input byte and current player state into facing, movement, pose, action, and animation requests
Inputs: normalized active-high control byte $7C (a set bit is a pressed direction or fire); death/condition latch $B6; player state $61,$65,$68/$69,$6C/$6D,$70,$89; decode tables at $97A4 and $9740
Outputs: updates desired direction $68, facing $69, action/motion $6C/$6D, pose $65, dirty flag $9F, and may select/install a player animation
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and player-control/animation scratch
Never reached: the instruction before ends with RTS, and no instruction, branch or pointer in this load names this address.

Continuation of $95F6 control interpretation: applies desired heading $68, allowing odd headings to replace $69 except an exact opposite; marks redraw $9F when changed. Sets movement $6C and derives facing/pose $65 and $6D. The $966F idle path clears $02B8 and may select an idle animation; $9699 onward handles changes in the fire/action state $78, comparing direction to facing before selecting an action through $9708. Uses $9740 and $97A4 direction lookups; no direct hardware writes. Entry is within the larger control routine, not an independent callable API.

Translate action code A into the Final Battle playable phase's player animation pointer and install that animation.
Inputs: A is the action code selected by the control logic (InterpretControls and InterpretNormalizedControls); $69 is player facing; phase animation lookup tables are valid.
Outputs: Stores A in $60, derives the facing-adjusted animation index, loads its pointer, initializes $60/$61/$5C/$58/$96/$5D, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $58, $5C/$5D, $60/$61, $6D, and $96.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes.

Install a new player animation-bytecode stream and prime its first control byte
Inputs: X = stream low byte; A = stream high byte; desired direction $68 and facing $69
Outputs: stores the stream pointer in $60/$61, loads its first byte into $5C, clears animation delay $58, copies $68 to $96, and stores $69 bit 1 in $5D
Clobbers: A, Y, and flags; X is preserved

Eight action-heading values 1,7,1,7,5,3,5,3 selected at $96F6. Index combines desired cardinal direction and current facing, then output replaces desired heading $68 before action animation selection. This is separate from the joystick low-nibble map $97A4.

Interpret the Final Battle playable phase's normalized control latch and update player motion/action animation state.
Inputs: $7C is the control byte normalized by ScanAndNormalizeInput ($874A); player animation, action, timing, facing, and collision state are current.
Outputs: Maps the low control nybble through the direction table at $97A4; a new direction, or none, restarts the hold timer $85, sets $88=$FF and sets $6D to the facing halved; once the same direction has been held for the delay from $979C (4 or 8 ticks) it selects action $84 x 4 + 8 (plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up) through SelectPlayerAnimationForAction, and again at once while the player's mode class is $10. The facing $69 is read, not written.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, player input/action/timing fields ($84, $85, $88, $6D), and animation-installation state on paths that select a new animation.
Hardware: No direct CIA or other hardware-register writes.

Eight alternating delays 4,8 indexed by normalized direction Y. $9775 compares elapsed tick difference against the chosen threshold before deriving action code $84*4+8, plus $20 when $70 is 0 or 4 and up, and selecting animation. This table controls action timing, not the joystick direction conversion.

16-entry map of the low four normalized control bits to eight directions 0..7 or $FF for no valid direction. $960F, $96BD and $974D use it to choose movement/facing/action; opposing direction combinations map to $FF. Fire occupies a different input bit and is handled separately.
PlayerAnimationPointers plus 1, the address the instruction at $9724 reads with Y as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

18 action-mode bases used at $9711: the action code A shifted right twice picks one, and the facing $69 shifted right once is added to it to give the player's action mode $6D, the value the control and combat code compares (as $6D with its low two bits masked) with $10, $0C and $24. The animation pointer at $97B4 is chosen separately, from A itself plus 0 or 2 for the facing. Values include $0C,$04,$18,$10,$1C,$14,$20,$28.

Build, advance, validate, and commit the player's movement candidate for this tick
Inputs: player position $54/$55 and its fractional bytes $50/$51; enemy position $56/$57; desired direction $68; facing $69; elapsed steps $8F; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: initializes candidate $48-$4D and opposing position $C9/$CA, calls AdvanceCandidate, commits candidate position and fractions back to $54/$55,$50/$51, and reports vertical displacement through the shared tail at $98D1 with X=0
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA

Build and advance the enemy movement candidate, record collision outcomes, and commit it only inside the playable bounds
Inputs: enemy position $56/$57 and its fractional bytes $52/$53; player position $54/$55; desired direction $6A; facing $6B; elapsed steps $8F; profile selector $D3; direction-mask table $1DA5
Outputs: updates candidate/collision scratch; records collision in $02B0/$02B2/$02B4 or failure count $02B1; commits $56/$57,$52/$53 only for X in [$02,$F6] and Y in [$09,$BC]; reports vertical displacement through $98D1 with X=2
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and candidate/collision scratch including $1E,$48-$4D,$C9/$CA,$CD

Add the signed number in A to the actor's $74,X, unless $EF is set or $74,X is 0 or $FF. A positive sum is held at $FF; a negative one is not held at zero but wraps, since the BCS at $98F0 goes on to the next instruction either way. Inputs: A, and X the actor's offset. Outputs: $74,X. Clobbers: A and flags; X and Y are kept.

Run the enemy animation interpreter once when the IRQ tick has advanced
Inputs: current tick $E2, enemy animation stamp $026E, and the already-installed enemy animation stream/state at actor offset 2
Outputs: if no tick elapsed, returns unchanged; otherwise stores elapsed delta in $8F, stamps $026E, sets X=2, and tail-enters the shared animation interpreter
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $8F, $026E, and all animation-interpreter scratch/state on the admitted path

Interpret one elapsed step of the selected actor's animation bytecode, including delay, pose, coordinate deltas, event generation, and continuation
Inputs: X=0 at $990A for player or X=2 at $990C for enemy; pointer $60/$61,X; control/delay $5C/$58-$59,X; actor position $54/$55,X; elapsed ticks $8F
Outputs: advances delay and stream position, updates pose $65,X, position $54/$55,X, event $64,X, continuation pointer, movement flags, and recomposes the actor's logical sprites when required
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and animation, movement, event, collision, and sprite-composition scratch

Run the Final Battle playable phase's animation interpreter for the scheduled enemy slot.
Inputs: X is the enemy animation-state offset selected by the scheduler (normally 2); $61,X is its stream pointer high byte; timing and animation state are current.
Outputs: Honors animation delay, decodes one bytecode step when due, updates the enemy animation/movement/event state, composes the resulting actor frame when requested, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $02/$03, animation timing/pointer/state bytes for slot X, actor-frame/sprite scratch, and event state selected by the bytecode.
Hardware: No direct hardware-register writes; bytecode paths requesting composition alter sprite work buffers and change CPU-port banking transiently before restoring it.

Compose an actor's current frame and hide the parts behind the area's foreground pictures. Inputs: X and $4F the actor offset (0 player, 2 enemy) and current animation frame $65,X; the mirror flag is $5D,X when $5C,X bit 4 is set, else $5C,X bit 6; depth $74,X. Outputs: the player is composed into sprite slots 0-3 with ComposeSprites, the enemy into slots 4-7 with ComposeEnemySprites; MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery then clears the sprite pixels behind the foreground pictures and stages the slots in $0240-$025F. X is not restored: it returns as 4 for the player and 8 for the enemy. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and shared renderer scratch. Hardware: it writes no chip register itself; the composer it calls switches the I/O area out through the processor port $01 while it reads the packed sprites and puts it back, and MaskActorSpritesBehindScenery stages the slots with interrupts off and ends with CLI.

Return immediately from the Final Battle playable phase's animation interpreter on the shared no-further-work path.
Inputs: The preceding animation branch has completed or determined that no frame composition is needed.
Outputs: Returns to the interpreter's caller without additional state or hardware changes.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and memory are preserved; RTS advances SP by two over the caller's return frame.
Delay for the requested number of engine ticks. Inputs: A is the tick count. Outputs: the requested tick transitions have elapsed. Clobbers: A, X, flags, and wait scratch.

Advance an actor candidate by up to eight elapsed substeps and test each proposed segment against compiled collision geometry
Inputs: X = the mover's facing index ($69 or $6B shifted right once, 0-3); Y = movement-profile selector; old/candidate position $48-$4B; candidate fractional bytes $4C/$4D; direction mask $1E; elapsed count $8F
Outputs: stores profile in $027F and capped count in $8E; updates candidate coordinates; returns collision and trigger state through $23/$24,$80/$81,$CD and related movement scratch
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags and broad candidate/collision scratch

Four negative-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $9A14 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate X, held at 0. Values $70,$C1,$70,$C1.

Four positive-X masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $9A2E in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, the profile's X step ($11DD,Y low, $11E7,Y high) is added to the candidate X, held at $FE. Values $07,$1C,$07,$1C.

Four negative-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $9A48 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $9B21 does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is subtracted from the candidate Y. Values $07,$C1,$07,$C1.

Four positive-Y masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $9A84 in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask, and the horizontal guard at $9B21 does not match, the profile's Y step ($11E2,Y low, $11EC,Y high) is added to the candidate Y. Values $70,$1C,$70,$1C.

Four vertical guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $9A65 and $9AA1 in AdvanceCandidate after a Y step. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the same Y step is applied twice more, three times in all. All four are $11, directions 0 and 4.

Four horizontal guard masks, one per facing index (the facing $69 or $6B shifted right once), read at $9A4F and $9A8B in AdvanceCandidate. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the Y step is skipped. All four are $44, directions 2 and 6.

Four walk-cycle masks, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $9594 in PlayerDriver. Each holds the three directions around that facing: $07 directions 0-2, $1C 2-4, $70 4-6, $C1 6, 7 and 0. When the direction bit in $1E is in the mask the walk frame (the low three bits of $65) steps forward by one, otherwise back by one.

Four mirror flags, one per facing index (the player's facing $69 shifted right once), read at $95BF. The flag, ANDed with the direction bit in $1E, is passed to ComposeSprites as its mirror flag $F1, so facing indexes 1 and 3 draw the frame mirrored. Values $00,$FF,$00,$FF.

Run object mode 5 for the player, then resolve actor overlap and dispatch the resulting player/enemy damage and reaction.

Restore an actor's saved mode, derive its facing/pose code, and perform channel-specific follow-up.

Admit and dispatch one active-opponent AI step, or route collision/boundary state to recovery
Inputs: active-enemy sign latch $CB; collision/boundary fields $02B0-$02B2; AI state $CF; timer slot 12; target-minus-one table beginning at $9ED1
Outputs: inactive enemies return; collision/boundary state jumps to recovery at $A20E; admitted normal state dispatches the selected AI handler by stack/RTS
Clobbers: A, X, flags, two stack bytes, and handler-dependent state; Y is preserved until the handler

16 words, one for each state of an enemy's fighting mind from state 0 up, each the address of that state's routine less one: the dispatcher pushes it and returns into it. AiDispatchTable plus 1, the address the instruction at $9EC5 reads with X as the index: the high byte of each word of the table, the index counting in pairs from the low byte.

Set the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 4 plus its facing $6B shifted right once; this is AI state 0's handler in the table at $9ED1.
Inputs: Current opponent facing $6B.
Outputs: Stores floor(($6B + 8)/2), which is 4 + $6B/2, in $6F and returns.
Clobbers: A and flags; $6F.

Set the Final Battle opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus its facing through the common tail at $9EF7.
Inputs: $6B is the current opponent facing/direction code.
Outputs: Computes $6F=(2*0+$6B)/2, mode class 0 plus the facing halved, and returns with it stored in $6F.
Clobbers: A, N, Z, C, and $6F; X and Y are preserved.

Set the opponent's action mode. Inputs: A is the mode class (0, 4, 8, an attack class $14-$20, or $24 for defeat) and $6B is the opponent's facing. Outputs: $6F = A + $6B/2, the class plus the facing halved, the same layout as the player's $6D. Clobbers: A, flags, and $6F.

Initialize a timed AI decision state and its random delay.
Inputs: AI option byte $D0 bit 6, tick $E2, current heading $6B, and random source $A631.
Outputs: Sets state $CF to 3 or 4, snapshots tick to $0275, stores random delay 0..31 in $CC, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0275, $CC, $6F, and random-source scratch.

Wait for the AI delay to expire, then enter state 5 with a rebuilt heading/action.
Inputs: Current tick $E2, delay origin $0275, delay $CC, current heading $6B, and helper state.
Outputs: Before expiry returns unchanged; at expiry sets $CF=5, derives and stores a new heading in $6A/$6B, invokes setup $A45B with X=8, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Face the opponent into the player's current relative quadrant and enter approach state 5.
Inputs: Player high-byte coordinates $54/$55 and opponent high-byte coordinates $56/$57; opponent heading and action fields.
Outputs: Sets AI state $CF=5, stores the quadrant classification returned by $A443 into both $6B (current heading) and $6A (desired heading), installs direction action class 8 through $A45B with X=8, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved through $9EF7, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, processor flags, $6A/$6B/$6F/$CF and helper scratch.

After the timed delay, choose a two-step heading turn, enter state 2, and begin horizontal-travel tracking.
Inputs: Tick/delay fields $E2/$0275/$CC, random source, heading $6B, and opponent X $56.
Outputs: At expiry sets $CF=2, rotates $6A/$6B by +2 or -2 modulo 8, snapshots $56 in $D1, runs setup X=$18, sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved, then continues into the travel tracker at $9F68.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, $D1, and helper scratch.

Track horizontal displacement from $D1, escalate after at least $14 units, and fall back to state 5 when the range test drops below $70.
Inputs: Opponent heading $6B, current X $56, baseline X $D1, tick $E2, and distance helper $A421.
Outputs: At sufficient directed displacement sets $CF=$0C, snapshots tick, calls setup X=4, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved; independently, a helper result below $70 resets through the state-5 entry at $9F21, which sets $CF=5 and turns $6A/$6B toward the player.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $0275, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Twelve ticks after state $0C began, enter state $0F, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state; it fires once, since state $0F has its own handler.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275, heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 12 ticks returns; afterward updates $0275, sets $CF=$0F, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=4, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 0 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $0275, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Six ticks after state $0F began, enter state 2, rotate opponent heading by two modulo 8, and rebuild movement state; it fires once, since state 2 has its own handler.
Inputs: Tick $E2, last tick $0275 (written when state $0F began, and not updated here), heading $6B, and movement helper state.
Outputs: Before 6 ticks returns; afterward sets $CF=2, writes ($6B+2)&7 to $6A/$6B, calls setup X=$18, and sets the opponent's action mode $6F to mode class 8 plus the facing halved.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $CF, $6A/$6B/$6F, and helper scratch.

Steer the enemy toward the player. Inputs: the player's position ($54/$55) and joystick heading $68, the enemy's position ($56/$57) and heading $6B, its profile $72 and behaviour $CB, the positions kept in $028A/$028B and $028E/$028F, and the tick $E2. It aims at a point level with the player, as far to one side as the profile's entry in $A3ED says, on the side the enemy is on, judged against the player's X less 8 when $68 is 0 to 3, plus 8 when it is 4 to 7, or unchanged when $68 is negative. When that point is less than 6 away from the enemy (Manhattan distance), or when the point would fall off the screen, it goes to RetargetAiToPlayer ($A029): that keeps the player's position in $028A/$028B, faces the enemy toward the player and enters state 6. It also holds the enemy's X between 4 and $F7, retargeting when it has to. With $CB at $80 and the player 56 or more away, it enters state 9 when the player is at least as far from the position in $028E/$028F as the enemy is (half the X distance plus half the Y distance each), and keeps the player's position there. Otherwise, when the heading toward the point and the heading toward the player differ in bit 2, it retargets one time in 16 (a random byte below $10) if the player is less than 8 away vertically. Then it turns the enemy toward the point (a turn that changes bit 2 of the heading waits until 20 ticks have passed since the last, kept in $02BE) and sets the heading $6A from the table at $A3F4: the entry before $6B when a quarter of the horizontal distance to the point is less than the vertical one, the entry for $6B when the vertical distance is under 4, and $6B itself otherwise. Outputs: $6A, $6B, $6F, $CF and the enemy's action. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1C-$21, $56, $028A/$028B, $028E/$028F, $02BE and the random-number state $F9-$FB.

Retarget the Final Battle playable phase's opponent AI to the player's current coordinates.
Inputs: Player coordinates are $54/$55 and the enemy's are $56/$57.
Outputs: Copies $54/$55 to $028A/$028B, sets $6A/$6B to the diagonal heading from the enemy toward the player (ClassifyRelativeActorQuadrant), installs that heading's action from the table at $A48B (InstallAiActionByDirection with X=4), sets $6F to mode class 0 plus the heading (the heading shifted right once), sets $CF=6, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), processor flags, $1F, the enemy's animation fields $5A/$5B/$5E/$5F/$62/$63, $028A/$028B, $6A/$6B/$6F, and $CF.
Hardware: No hardware registers are read or written.

Choose between an immediate recovery/timer state and a randomized attack setup from the player's current actor mode.
Inputs: Player actor mode $6D, behavior selector $72, tick $E2, random source, opponent heading $6B, and AI sequence counter $02BD.
Outputs: If ($6D&$FC)==$24, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5; otherwise selects a bounded random action/setup, sets $CF=7, and increments $02BD.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0 on the attack path), flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, $6F, $02BD, the random-number state $F9-$FB, and helper scratch.

Choose and install a random close-range opponent action for the Final Battle playable phase.
Inputs: Opponent/player proximity tests have reached the close-range branch; the enemy's profile $72 (zero allows two variants, nonzero four), its heading $6B, animation state, and PRNG are current.
Outputs: Selects a bounded random variant, installs its animation/heading parameters through the phase helpers, sets $CF=7, increments $02BD, and returns.
Clobbers: A, X, Y (left 0), processor flags, PRNG state $F9-$FB, helper scratch, action/animation state, $CF, and $02BD.

Wait for the opponent animation pointer high byte to clear, then initialize AI state 8 timing.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63, tick $E2, and random source.
Outputs: Returns while $63 is nonzero; when zero, sets $CF=8, snapshots $E2 to $0276, and stores a random byte in $D5.
Clobbers: A, flags, $CF, $0276, $D5, and random-source scratch.

Decide whether the player is close enough to the AI target for a scripted action. Inputs: player coordinates, $028A/$028B target coordinates, and AI state and timers. Outputs: proximity and action state are updated and an AI path may be entered. Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, and AI scratch.

Wait for both opponent animation completion and projectile slot 1 inactivity, then reset through AI state 5.
Inputs: Opponent animation pointer high byte $63 and projectile slot-1 state $0281.
Outputs: Returns if either field is nonzero; when both are zero, tail-enters the state-5 reset at $9F21.
Clobbers: A, flags, and on reset A/X/Y (Y left 0) plus $CF/$6A/$6B/$6F, $1F, the enemy's animation fields and helper scratch.

Return at once, for state 10, the one enemy state that does nothing (its word in the dispatch table at $9ED1 is $A1AF). Its RTS returns to the code that called OpponentAI: the address the dispatcher pushed at $9EC5-$9ECC was used up by the RTS at $9ECD that jumped here. Inputs and outputs: none. Clobbers: nothing.

Let a defeated enemy get up again once its energy has refilled (AI state 11, which SpawnEnemy sets for an enemy restored as defeated and event 3 sets when the defeat animation $B61D or $B629 reaches it).
Inputs: Area index $A2, the area's defeat byte $012D,X, the ticks $E2/$F0 and the defeat time $0175,X/$0187,X, player/opponent positions $54-$57, heading $6B, and animation pointers $B63F/$B635.
Outputs: Returns at once while $012D,X is $FF (beaten for good). Otherwise rebuilds the enemy's energy from the ticks since its defeat (RebuildEnemyMeterFromElapsedTicks, which writes $022A and $3F92,X); when that has reached 44 and the player is not within 12 horizontally and 6 vertically, puts the candles out in area 1 (PutOutCandles, $A1E5), clears bit 7 of $012D,X, sets $CF=7, installs the animation at $B63F (heading bit 2 clear) or $B635 (bit 2 set) through InstallAiScript ($9E22), and writes $0236=6; otherwise returns without transition.
Clobbers: A, X, Y, flags, $1E/$1F, $022A, $3F92,X, and when the enemy gets up $012D,X, $CF, enemy animation state $5A/$5E/$62/$63, and $0236, and in area 1 the candle bytes $029F-$02A3.
